thread:
Alex: kicking off canary for sandstorm20b-v1-int4. seeing OOMs during warm multi-turns when users ask long followups. p50 looks fine but p99 OOMs on KV alloc. paste short log: 

Alex: ```
[2026-04-01T08:22:14Z] serve: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
model=sandstorm20b-v1-int4 shard=5 seq_len=512 batch=1 new_tokens=210
KV_pct=85 slab_frag=0.48
stack: runtime/serve.cu:401 alloc_kv.cu:102
```

Nora: ouch. what's the current canary config (microbatch/prefetch/max_new_tokens/slot_reserve)?

Alex: canary config:```
model: sandstorm20b-v1-int4
replicas: 6
microbatch_size: 2
batch_timeout_ms: 12
prefetch: aggressive
max_new_tokens_default: 256
slot_reserve: 0.07
soft_evict: false
kernel_pref: "speed"
```

Derek: that slab_frag=0.48 + aggressive prefetch explains it. two levers: reduce peak allocations (lower max_new_tokens + microbatch), and increase allocator cushion (slot_reserve + soft_evict + kv_trim). Also consider microbatch_join_ms to smooth pulses. Proposed canary overrides:```
rollout set sandstorm20b.canary {
  overrides: {
    prefetch: "streamed",
    microbatch_size: 1,
    microbatch_join_ms: 8,
    batch_timeout_ms: 8,
    max_new_tokens_default: 96,
    slot_reserve: 0.20,
    soft_evict: true,
    kv_trim_pct: 0.30,
    kernel_pref: "memory-lean"
  }
}
```

infra-bot: ALERT: node-gpu-5 OOM at 2026-04-01T08:21:59Z while running sandstorm-canary-5. free_mem dropped below 350MB.

Nora: agree with Derek. microbatch=1 will likely nudge p50 up slightly; microbatch_join_ms=8 should help tails. Also lower max_new_tokens to 96 for the canary since many customer flows don't need 256.

Alex: before we patch, let's snapshot slab counters and nvprof mem trace for shard 5. Can we run slab_snap and memprofile hooks? Also run a quick quant-quality eval after changes.

bench-bot: queued: eval run-id sandstorm-canary-6200 when started. Use conversational-smoke + adversarial-longform.

Derek: eval command we use:```
./eval_harness --model sandstorm20b-v1-int4 --baseline sandstorm20b-v1-int8 --evalset conversational-smoke,adversarial-longform --metrics semantic_sim,rouge --run-id sandstorm-canary-6200 --save-diffs
```
If semantic_sim drops >1.5% abort and fallback to int8. Also run a 10k A/B with fallback rule to 20% traffic if stable.

QA-Maya: I'll own the A/B and diffs. After rollout completes I will run 10k requests (mix of short+long turns) and record semantic_sim, latency, and slab_frag every 15s. ETA ~2h.

Alex: plan: 1) snapshot slab+nvprof 2) apply conservative overrides Derek suggested 3) run quant eval + 10k A/B 4) monitor for 60m stable. Who can push the rollout?

Nora: I can push the patch now and add the snapshot hooks to the runbook. Pushing in 30s and watching prometheus dash: http://dash.internal/ml/sandstorm/canary-6200 (mem/cuda_free, slab_frag, p99_lat).

Derek: if OOMs persist after conservative changes, fallback options: increase slot_reserve to 0.30, enable kv_sparse_trim=0.4, temporarily reduce canary traffic to 5%, and consider per-shard kernel tuning. But try the lighter touch first.
